# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']
    types: [completed]
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge-trigger.yml@main

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Per guidelines: "CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)". Hmm. The rule says CI failures should be treated as blocking. But the verdict rules say BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI)... The red CI here is the merge bot run failing due to GitHub API rate limit — an infra flake, unrelated to the PR diff. But the guidelines are explicit: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)".

Hmm, but there's tension: flagging this PR as REQUEST_CHANGES because an unrelated bot run hit a rate limit would trigger a rework round that can't fix anything (the rework can't fix GitHub's rate limit). The verdict rules also warn about wasted rounds. But the instruction is explicit and mechanical: CI failures → BLOCKING.

Let me think about this more carefully. The verdict rules say: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss." A red CI gate is listed. And formatting rule F7: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING".

But also the machine cross-check: "The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments... if any finding is truly blocking, set recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking: 1+".

So mechanically: ci_failures.md present → each failure as BLOCKING → blocking >= 1 → REQUEST_CHANGES. Hmm, but is that the right engineering outcome? The failure is a rate-limit in the merge bot infrastructure, which is transient. A rework round would just re-run.

Hold on — let me check whether the failure is really transient/unrelated, or whether the merge bot failure is actually BECAUSE of this PR. The failed run was for commit 4818ea69 (the PR head merge commit). The merge bot runs on check_run completion / PR events. It failed in resolve_tag with rate limit. That's clearly environmental: "API rate limit exceeded for user ID 236856673" — the bot user exhausted its API quota. Nothing in the PR diff affects the merge bot.

However — there's a legitimate review concern here that's IN scope for this PR: **the new badge step adds more API calls on every main-side run**? No wait, the badge step uses git push, not API. The gh CLI calls... `gh release view` etc. already existed. The new step doesn't add gh API calls. Fine.

But hmm, let me also review deeper for actual issues in the diff. Let me carefully review the new code:

### Step 1: `crap-all.txt` generation in "Update the released baseline" step

```yaml
# Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
"$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
```

Observations:
1. This runs a THIRD full crap4js analysis (ratchet step ran one, update-baseline runs another). Performance: three full analyses per main run. It's CI, cosmetic. SUGGESTION level: could derive the full report from the existing runs (e.g., run `--threshold 999` once and derive the ratchet verdict from it — though the tooling may not support that). Or reuse the update.txt report? The update runs with threshold CRAP_THRESHOLD so it only reports functions over threshold. The full report needs all functions. OK, so a third run is needed unless the tool supports multiple outputs. It's acceptable, minor perf note.

2. `|| true` — swallows failure; if crap-all.txt is empty/missing, the badge step's `fs.readFileSync` throws → the whole node script fails → `continue-on-error: true` → step marked failed (with continue-on-error, step shows as failed but job continues? Actually continue-on-error marks the step as failed (red X) but the job succeeds... The conclusion of the step is failure but outcome success? With continue-on-error: true, the step's `outcome` is failure but `conclusion` is success, and the job continues, job passes). The job shows a red X on the step? Actually with continue-on-error, GitHub shows the step with a red X but the workflow run itself is green? No — continue-on-error at step level: step conclusion = success (so job is green), but outcome = failure; the UI shows the step with a red X annotation "Error: Process completed with exit code 1" but the job passes. Hmm, actually I recall the step shows as failed-with-continue (red X) and the run is green. This is deliberate ("cosmetic — never fails the pipeline"). OK.

3. Order-of-operations correctness: the crap-all.txt is generated in the "Update the released baseline" step. The badge step runs AFTER it. The badge step's `if:` condition matches the update step's condition (same expression) — EXCEPT: the update step also `exit 0`s early when "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)". In that early-exit path, crap-all.txt WAS generated (line runs before the if). Good — the generation happens before the early exit. ✓.

4. But wait — there's a real bug candidate: the update step's condition is `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')`. The badge step uses the identical condition. Fine.

   BUT: consider `workflow_dispatch` on a PR head (the SM dispatches validation on PR heads). `github.ref != refs/heads/main` → badge step skipped. ✓ main only.

5. **The bigger issue — `git push` to `badges` branch and `GITHUB_TOKEN`**: The workflow has `permissions: contents: write` at top level, so pushing with github.token works. BUT: can you push to a repository with GITHUB_TOKEN from a workflow triggered by `workflow_run`? Yes, contents:write allows it. One caveat: if the repo has branch protection on `badges`, push fails — continue-on-error covers it.

6. **`GITHUB_TOKEN` in URL vs env**: `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/...` — the token lands in the git remote URL / process args. GitHub auto-masks secrets in logs; but if git errors, the URL could be printed... git redacts the password in "unable to access" messages (git ≥ 2.3? there were fixes; modern git masks credentials in error output — actually git strips userinfo when printing URLs in errors since 2.x? Let me not overstate: there WAS a known issue where tokens leak in error messages, fixed by redacting. Modern git redacts). Also the token persists in `.git/config`? No — it's a one-shot push URL, not saved. It IS passed as a command-line argument to git, visible in `ps` on the runner — standard practice, low risk on ephemeral runners. A cleaner way: `git push https://${GH_TOKEN}@...` or use `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic ..."`. This is SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level nit. Most workflows do exactly this. I'd call it SUGGESTION.

7. **README badges link raw.githubusercontent.com on the `badges` branch** — for a public repo this works. But `raw.githubusercontent.com` serves with `content-type: text/plain`... shields.io endpoint badges require the JSON endpoint; raw.githubusercontent serves JSON files as text/plain but shields accepts it (they parse regardless? shields endpoint badge requires schemaVersion JSON; shields fetches server-side and parses — content-type text/plain is fine; this is the standard documented pattern: `https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/...` — yes, standard pattern used widely). ✓.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

`          git push -q -f "https://x-access-token:${G...`

The prefix shown by grep -o is `x-access-token:${G` — so the actual content is `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/...` or `${GH_TOKEN}` etc. The length of the secret portion (between `x-access-token:` and `@github`) is 11 characters INCLUDING a trailing newline handling... Yes! `${GH_TOKEN}` is exactly 11 chars: `$`, `{`, `G`, `H`, `_`, `T`, `O`, `K`, `E`, `N`, `}` = 11.

So the actual line is:
```
git push -q -f "https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" badges
```

Note: there's a subtlety — using `x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}` in a URL: GH_TOKEN contains the token; that's standard practice for pushing via HTTPS. The token will be visible in the process listing / potentially in error messages (git may echo the URL with credentials in some error paths, though git redacts credentials in most errors... ===
diff --git a/.github/workflows/quality.yml b/.github/workflows/quality.yml
index 588fa083..aa5741f5 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/quality.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/quality.yml
@@ -170,6 +170,8 @@ jobs:
           NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
           OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
           mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
+          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
+          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
           if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
             cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
             "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
@@ -196,6 +198,47 @@ jobs:
           gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
           echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
 
+      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)
+        # Dynamic shields.io endpoint badges: the numbers come from this run, the JSON lives on an
+        # orphan 'badges' branch, so nothing in the code tree changes (no PR conflicts, no bot
+        # commits on main). Cosmetic — never fails the pipeline.
+        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
+        continue-on-error: true
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+        run: |
+          set -e
+          node - <<'JS'
+          const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
+          const tmp = process.env.RUNNER_TEMP, thr = Number(process.env.CRAP_THRESHOLD);
+          const cov = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'cov/coverage-final.json'), 'utf8'));
+          let t = 0, h = 0;
+          for (const [f, e] of Object.entries(cov)) {
+            if (/\/(unit-tests|test)\//.test(f)) continue;       // product code only
+            for (const k in e.s) { t++; if (e.s[k] > 0) h++; }
+          }
+          const report = fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'crap-all.txt'), 'utf8');
+          const rows = report.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim().split(/\s+/)).filter((c) => c.length >= 5 && /\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(c[1]) && !/\/(unit-tests|test)\//.test(c[1]) && !isNaN(parseFloat(c[c.length - 1])));
+          const scores = rows.map((c) => parseFloat(c[c.length - 1]));
+          const max = Math.max(0, ...scores), over = scores.filter((x) => x > thr).length;
+          const pct = t ? Math.round((1000 * h) / t) / 10 : 0;
+          const colorMax = max <= 12 ? 'brightgreen' : max <= 30 ? 'yellow' : max <= 200 ? 'orange' : 'red';
+          const colorOver = over === 0 ? 'brightgreen' : over <= 25 ? 'yellow' : over <= 150 ? 'orange' : 'red';
+          const colorCov = pct >= 90 ? 'brightgreen' : pct >= 80 ? 'green' : pct >= 70 ? 'yellowgreen' : pct >= 50 ? 'yellow' : 'orange';
+          const out = path.join(tmp, 'badges');
+          fs.mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
+          const w = (n, label, message, color) => fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, n), JSON.stringify({ schemaVersion: 1, label, message, color }) + '\n');
+          w('crap-max.json', 'CRAP max', String(Math.round(max * 10) / 10), colorMax);
+          w('crap-over.json', `CRAP > ${thr}`, `${over} fns`, colorOver);
+          w('coverage.json', 'coverage', `${pct}%`, colorCov);
+          console.log(`badges: max=${max} over=${over} coverage=${pct}%`);
+          JS
+          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/badges"
+          git init -q && git checkout -q -b badges
+          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'; git config user.email 'github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
+          git add -A && git commit -q -m "badges: main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
+          git push -q -f "https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" badges
+

         env:

# Merge Trigger — thin stub over the canonical pr_approved merge bot
# (dmtools-agentic-workflows). Event triggers stay repo-side: this repo's
# validation CI is `Quality` and it fires on PR heads automatically
# (pull_request trigger), so the bot only merges CLEAN, green PRs.
name: Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : Quality passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']
    types: [completed]
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge-trigger.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-24.04
      remove_pr_label: true
      map_pr_labels: true
      gh_branch_pattern: true
    secrets: inherit
======
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

The CI failure root cause: **GitHub API rate limit exceeded** (`gh: API rate limit exceeded for user ID 236856673... HTTP 403`) in the merge bot's `resolve_tag` step — infrastructure/rate-limit issue in the external `factory-merge.yml` reusable workflow, **not** caused by this PR's changes. The PR only touches `quality.yml` (a badge-publishing step) and `README.md` (badge images).

Per guidelines: "CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)". Hmm. The rule says CI failures should be treated as blocking. But the verdict rules say BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI)... The red CI here is the merge bot run failing due to GitHub API rate limit — an infra flake, unrelated to the PR diff. But the guidelines are explicit: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)".

Hmm, but there's tension: flagging this PR as REQUEST_CHANGES because an unrelated bot run hit a rate limit would trigger a rework round that can't fix anything (the rework can't fix GitHub's rate limit). The verdict rules also warn about wasted rounds. But the instruction is explicit and mechanical: CI failures → BLOCKING.

Let me think about this more carefully. The verdict rules say: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss." A red CI gate is listed. And formatting rule F7: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING".

But also the machine cross-check: "The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments... if any finding is truly blocking, set recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking: 1+".

So mechanically: ci_failures.md present → each failure as BLOCKING → blocking >= 1 → REQUEST_CHANGES. Hmm, but is that the right engineering outcome? The failure is a rate-limit in the merge bot infrastructure, which is transient. A rework round would just re-run.

Hold on — let me check whether the failure is really transient/unrelated, or whether the merge bot failure is actually BECAUSE of this PR. The failed run was for commit 4818ea69 (the PR head merge commit). The merge bot runs on check_run completion / PR events. It failed in resolve_tag with rate limit. That's clearly environmental: "API rate limit exceeded for user ID 236856673" — the bot user exhausted its API quota. Nothing in the PR diff affects the merge bot.

However — there's a legitimate review concern here that's IN scope for this PR: **the new badge step adds more API calls on every main-side run**? No wait, the badge step uses git push, not API. The gh CLI calls... `gh release view` etc. already existed. The new step doesn't add gh API calls. Fine.

But hmm, let me also review deeper for actual issues in the diff. Let me carefully review the new code:

### Step 1: `crap-all.txt` generation in "Update the released baseline" step

```yaml
# Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
"$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
```

Observations:
1. This runs a THIRD full crap4js analysis (ratchet step ran one, update-baseline runs another). Performance: three full analyses per main run. It's CI, cosmetic. SUGGESTION level: could derive the full report from the existing runs (e.g., run `--threshold 999` once and derive the ratchet verdict from it — though the tooling may not support that). Or reuse the update.txt report? The update runs with threshold CRAP_THRESHOLD so it only reports functions over threshold. The full report needs all functions. OK, so a third run is needed unless the tool supports multiple outputs. It's acceptable, minor perf note.

2. `|| true` — swallows failure; if crap-all.txt is empty/missing, the badge step's `fs.readFileSync` throws → the whole node script fails → `continue-on-error: true` → step marked failed (with continue-on-error, step shows as failed but job continues? Actually continue-on-error marks the step as failed (red X) but the job succeeds... The conclusion of the step is failure but outcome success? With continue-on-error: true, the step's `outcome` is failure but `conclusion` is success, and the job continues, job passes). The job shows a red X on the step? Actually with continue-on-error, GitHub shows the step with a red X but the workflow run itself is green? No — continue-on-error at step level: step conclusion = success (so job is green), but outcome = failure; the UI shows the step with a red X annotation "Error: Process completed with exit code 1" but the job passes. Hmm, actually I recall the step shows as failed-with-continue (red X) and the run is green. This is deliberate ("cosmetic — never fails the pipeline"). OK.

3. Order-of-operations correctness: the crap-all.txt is generated in the "Update the released baseline" step. The badge step runs AFTER it. The badge step's `if:` condition matches the update step's condition (same expression) — EXCEPT: the update step also `exit 0`s early when "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)". In that early-exit path, crap-all.txt WAS generated (line runs before the if). Good — the generation happens before the early exit. ✓.

4. But wait — there's a real bug candidate: the update step's condition is `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')`. The badge step uses the identical condition. Fine.

   BUT: consider `workflow_dispatch` on a PR head (the SM dispatches validation on PR heads). `github.ref != refs/heads/main` → badge step skipped. ✓ main only.

5. **The bigger issue — `git push` to `badges` branch and `GITHUB_TOKEN`**: The workflow has `permissions: contents: write` at top level, so pushing with github.token works. BUT: can you push to a repository with GITHUB_TOKEN from a workflow triggered by `workflow_run`? Yes, contents:write allows it. One caveat: if the repo has branch protection on `badges`, push fails — continue-on-error covers it.

6. **`GITHUB_TOKEN` in URL vs env**: `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/...` — the token lands in the git remote URL / process args. GitHub auto-masks secrets in logs; but if git errors, the URL could be printed... git redacts the password in "unable to access" messages (git ≥ 2.3? there were fixes; modern git masks credentials in error output — actually git strips userinfo when printing URLs in errors since 2.x? Let me not overstate: there WAS a known issue where tokens leak in error messages, fixed by redacting. Modern git redacts). Also the token persists in `.git/config`? No — it's a one-shot push URL, not saved. It IS passed as a command-line argument to git, visible in `ps` on the runner — standard practice, low risk on ephemeral runners. A cleaner way: `git push https://${GH_TOKEN}@...` or use `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic ..."`. This is SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level nit. Most workflows do exactly this. I'd call it SUGGESTION.

7. **README badges link raw.githubusercontent.com on the `badges` branch** — for a public repo this works. But `raw.githubusercontent.com` serves with `content-type: text/plain`... shields.io endpoint badges require the JSON endpoint; raw.githubusercontent serves JSON files as text/plain but shields accepts it (they parse regardless? shields endpoint badge requires schemaVersion JSON; shields fetches server-side and parses — content-type text/plain is fine; this is the standard documented pattern: `https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/...` — yes, standard pattern used widely). ✓.

8. **Badge staleness**: badges only update when the gate runs on main — i.e., when baseline doesn't cover HEAD. Fine.

9. **The coverage computation in the badge script vs crap4js report**: The badge script computes statement coverage from `coverage-final.json` — counts ALL statements in product files (excluding `/unit-tests/` and `/test/` dirs). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

# Merge Trigger — thin stub over the canonical pr_approved merge bot
# (dmtools-agentic-workflows). Event triggers stay repo-side: this repo's
# validation CI is `Quality` and it fires on PR heads automatically
# (pull_request trigger), so the bot only merges CLEAN, green PRs.
name: Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : Quality passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']
    types: [completed]
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge-trigger.yml@main
    with:
      runner: ubuntu-24.04
      remove_pr_label: true
      map_pr_labels: true
      gh_branch_pattern: true
    secrets: inherit
======
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

The CI failure root cause: **GitHub API rate limit exceeded** (`gh: API rate limit exceeded for user ID 236856673... HTTP 403`) in the merge bot's `resolve_tag` step — infrastructure/rate-limit issue in the external `factory-merge.yml` reusable workflow, **not** caused by this PR's changes. The PR only touches `quality.yml` (a badge-publishing step) and `README.md` (badge images).

Per guidelines: "CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)". Hmm. The rule says CI failures should be treated as blocking. But the verdict rules say BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI)... The red CI here is the merge bot run failing due to GitHub API rate limit — an infra flake, unrelated to the PR diff. But the guidelines are explicit: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)".

Hmm, but there's tension: flagging this PR as REQUEST_CHANGES because an unrelated bot run hit a rate limit would trigger a rework round that can't fix anything (the rework can't fix GitHub's rate limit). The verdict rules also warn about wasted rounds. But the instruction is explicit and mechanical: CI failures → BLOCKING.

Let me think about this more carefully. The verdict rules say: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss." A red CI gate is listed. And formatting rule F7: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING".

But also the machine cross-check: "The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments... if any finding is truly blocking, set recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking: 1+".

So mechanically: ci_failures.md present → each failure as BLOCKING → blocking >= 1 → REQUEST_CHANGES. Hmm, but is that the right engineering outcome? The failure is a rate-limit in the merge bot infrastructure, which is transient. A rework round would just re-run.

Hold on — let me check whether the failure is really transient/unrelated, or whether the merge bot failure is actually BECAUSE of this PR. The failed run was for commit 4818ea69 (the PR head merge commit). The merge bot runs on check_run completion / PR events. It failed in resolve_tag with rate limit. That's clearly environmental: "API rate limit exceeded for user ID 236856673" — the bot user exhausted its API quota. Nothing in the PR diff affects the merge bot.

However — there's a legitimate review concern here that's IN scope for this PR: **the new badge step adds more API calls on every main-side run**? No wait, the badge step uses git push, not API. The gh CLI calls... `gh release view` etc. already existed. The new step doesn't add gh API calls. Fine.

But hmm, let me also review deeper for actual issues in the diff. Let me carefully review the new code:

### Step 1: `crap-all.txt` generation in "Update the released baseline" step

```yaml
# Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
"$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
```

Observations:
1. This runs a THIRD full crap4js analysis (ratchet step ran one, update-baseline runs another). Performance: three full analyses per main run. It's CI, cosmetic. SUGGESTION level: could derive the full report from the existing runs (e.g., run `--threshold 999` once and derive the ratchet verdict from it — though the tooling may not support that). Or reuse the update.txt report? The update runs with threshold CRAP_THRESHOLD so it only reports functions over threshold. The full report needs all functions. OK, so a third run is needed unless the tool supports multiple outputs. It's acceptable, minor perf note.

2. `|| true` — swallows failure; if crap-all.txt is empty/missing, the badge step's `fs.readFileSync` throws → the whole node script fails → `continue-on-error: true` → step marked failed (with continue-on-error, step shows as failed but job continues? Actually continue-on-error marks the step as failed (red X) but the job succeeds... The conclusion of the step is failure but outcome success? With continue-on-error: true, the step's `outcome` is failure but `conclusion` is success, and the job continues, job passes). The job shows a red X on the step? Actually with continue-on-error, GitHub shows the step with a red X but the workflow run itself is green? No — continue-on-error at step level: step conclusion = success (so job is green), but outcome = failure; the UI shows the step with a red X annotation "Error: Process completed with exit code 1" but the job passes. Hmm, actually I recall the step shows as failed-with-continue (red X) and the run is green. This is deliberate ("cosmetic — never fails the pipeline"). OK.

3. Order-of-operations correctness: the crap-all.txt is generated in the "Update the released baseline" step. The badge step runs AFTER it. The badge step's `if:` condition matches the update step's condition (same expression) — EXCEPT: the update step also `exit 0`s early when "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)". In that early-exit path, crap-all.txt WAS generated (line runs before the if). Good — the generation happens before the early exit. ✓.

4. But wait — there's a real bug candidate: the update step's condition is `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')`. The badge step uses the identical condition. Fine.

   BUT: consider `workflow_dispatch` on a PR head (the SM dispatches validation on PR heads). `github.ref != refs/heads/main` → badge step skipped. ✓ main only.

5. **The bigger issue — `git push` to `badges` branch and `GITHUB_TOKEN`**: The workflow has `permissions: contents: write` at top level, so pushing with github.token works. BUT: can you push to a repository with GITHUB_TOKEN from a workflow triggered by `workflow_run`? Yes, contents:write allows it. One caveat: if the repo has branch protection on `badges`, push fails — continue-on-error covers it.

6. **`GITHUB_TOKEN` in URL vs env**: `https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/...` — the token lands in the git remote URL / process args. GitHub auto-masks secrets in logs; but if git errors, the URL could be printed... git redacts the password in "unable to access" messages (git ≥ 2.3? there were fixes; modern git masks credentials in error output — actually git strips userinfo when printing URLs in errors since 2.x? Let me not overstate: there WAS a known issue where tokens leak in error messages, fixed by redacting. Modern git redacts). Also the token persists in `.git/config`? No — it's a one-shot push URL, not saved. It IS passed as a command-line argument to git, visible in `ps` on the runner — standard practice, low risk on ephemeral runners. A cleaner way: `git push https://${GH_TOKEN}@...` or use `git -c http.extraheader="AUTHORIZATION: basic ..."`. This is SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level nit. Most workflows do exactly this. I'd call it SUGGESTION.

7. **README badges link raw.githubusercontent.com on the `badges` branch** — for a public repo this works. But `raw.githubusercontent.com` serves with `content-type: text/plain`... shields.io endpoint badges require the JSON endpoint; raw.githubusercontent serves JSON files as text/plain but shields accepts it (they parse regardless? shields endpoint badge requires schemaVersion JSON; shields fetches server-side and parses — content-type text/plain is fine; this is the standard documented pattern: `https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/...` — yes, standard pattern used widely). ✓.

8. **Badge staleness**: badges only update when the gate runs on main — i.e., when baseline doesn't cover HEAD. Fine.

9. **The coverage computation in the badge script vs crap4js report**: The badge script computes statement coverage from `coverage-final.json` — counts ALL statements in product files (excluding `/unit-tests/` and `/test/` dirs). All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4.
